backward_compat_traps.usb4: Carries USB3.2 as a TUNNEL over the transport layer, not natively.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A USB4 port still exposes native USB 2.0 on D+/D- and USB 3.2 via tunnel; mismatched assumptions about 'native' vs 'tunneled' USB3 break interop.
A Gen-2-only USB4 device negotiates 20 Gbps aggregate, not 40 Gbps — surprising users who expect '40 Gbps USB4'.

backward_compat_traps.usb4: Built on Thunderbolt 3 but TB3 interop is OPTIONAL.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Not every USB4 host certifies Thunderbolt 3 compatibility; a TB3 device may not work on a USB4 port that did not advertise TB3 interop.

backward_compat_traps.usb4_v2: Gen 4 PAM-3 multilevel signalling for 80 Gbps.
backward_compat_traps.trap: 80 Gbps requires USB4 v2 cabling + PHYs; older USB4 1.0 cables/ports cap at 40 Gbps.

previous_versions: Thunderbolt 3 (2015, Intel) — donated base protocol for USB4.
USB4 Version 1.0 (August 29, 2019) — 20 / 40 Gbps router-based tunneling fabric.
USB4 Version 2.0 (2022) — adds 80 Gbps symmetric / up to 120 Gbps asymmetric (Gen 4, PAM-3).

key_changes.summary: Intel's 40 Gbps tunneling protocol over USB-C; donated as the USB4 base.
USB-IF tunneling fabric: USB3/DP/PCIe tunnels, router topology, Connection Manager, 20/40 Gbps Gen 2/Gen 3.
Gen 4 PAM-3 signalling for 80 Gbps symmetric; asymmetric (3:1) lane mode up to 120 Gbps; enhanced DP/PCIe tunneling.

fields.version_naming_history_note: USB4 is maintained by the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF). Its base protocol is Thunderbolt 3, donated by Intel. USB4 1.0 was published August 29, 2019; USB4 2.0 (2022) added 80 Gbps. USB4 sits above earlier USB generations (USB 2.0 480 Mbps, USB 3.2 up to 20 Gbps) which it carries natively or via tunnels.
fields.ic_name: USB4 (USB Implementers Forum, Intel Thunderbolt 3 base)
